title: Saving documents in Draft Mode
text:
Saving documents in Draft Mode 
 N avigation in Farvision 
 Saving documents in draft mode 
 Draft mode allows users to temporarily save typed data without storing the data in the actual transactional database. Large transactions can be saved in interim state as Draft mode for future use. User can resume re-entry of transactions from draft mode. 
 Transactions within draft mode are not available for any further subsequent processing. Draft Mode has to be set as ‘ON’ in the interface for Draft mode saving button to be enabled. There is no such setting required for Draft mode enabling. It is enabled by code only. 
 ‘Save As Draft’ is enabled under submit menu. 
 After a document is saved as draft, user can only retrieve it again after making draft mode on in the same interface. 
 Click on the row to open the screen and make further entry or necessary changes. After that user is required to finally submit and save the entry. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Queue Management for Reports
text:
Queue Management for Reports 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Queue Management for Reports 
 Queue management allows for processing of data in the background so that the user does not have to wait while data is being processed. Once the report or process is completed a notification will be provided that the job has been completed. It is important to use queues so that server utilization is not disturbed during peak working hours. 
 There are two types of queues 
 Queue Reports 
 Queue Processes 
 Notifications 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of job. Report can be downloaded from the notification alert. Queue Reports 
Some reports and bulk print format can be queued. There are two types of processes 
 ● Fire and forget - the queue is started on demand when the report has to be processed 
 ● Repeat every few minutes - any data which is added for the bulk processing will be processed, and checking for new data will be done on a predefined frequency. 
 Fire and forget 
 A job id is assigned against reports which are being queued under fire and forget. A notification will be sent to the user’s device once the report is ready. Reports which have been queued can only be printed from the Queue management console. Queued reports cannot be printed (either PDF or Excel) from the menu interface from which generation of report was started. 
 Example : Application detail register, Booking register, Invoice register and Receipt register, Indent register, Purchase order register, Goods receipt Note register and Purchase Bill register. Examples for Bulk Printing of documents are Invoice, Booking annexure, Applicant Ledger. 
 Repeat every few minutes 
Queues which repeat every few minutes are used for bulk printing of documents. No job id assigned as it is a continuous loop where more documents which are added for bulk processes are picked up. After receiving the notification, search Bulk Printing in the menu column and then for the relevant menu Item. 
 Download : Once the report is complete, it can be downloaded and saved locally. The report will be automatically deleted after downloading. Reports will be visible in the queue console until the reports are downloaded. Users are allowed to download their reports while admin users can download report of any user. 
 Delete : Pending and generated report can be deleted. If the status is pending, the delete button will stop the processing of the report. If the status is Complete, delete will physically remove the report and it will not be available, it is deleted from the server. 
 Status : Pending, In Process, Complete, Error, No record found are the status of the queued report. 
 Remarks : This column provides details of the status. Example, For In process, it will show start. 
 Desktop notification will be shown after completion of the job. Hide Downloaded : On select of the Hide Downloaded check box, all downloaded row items will be hidden and only those row items will be shown which are pending for download. Queue Process 
 Some reports a process has to be run before the report can be generated. 
 Example : Finance module cash flow report generated through process method and process report will be downloaded from queue console under the Process tab. 
 Property management invoice generated through bulk invoice menu after notification will be downloaded from the queue console. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Data Import Process
text:
Data Import Process 
 Some common features of Farvision 
 Data Import Process 
 Data import allows data to be imported from excel sheets instead of entering through the interface. Data has to be entered in pre-defined excel sheets, checked for correctness and is then imported into Farvision. Data import is available for many masters and a few transactions, the process of importing is the same. Only the excel template is different in which data has to be entered. 
 Data import is normally used by first time users of Farvision, or if there is a huge volume. Bulk data can be inserted into Farvision and it saves time. Once your backlog is cleared, it is recommended to use the interface for day to day entry. Sometimes data import is also used where the number of rows in a document is very large, example a journal voucher with 200 lines. 
 There are four steps to be followed 
 ● Download Template 
 ● Upload Template 
 ● Validate Data 
 ● Import Data 
 DOWNLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Object: This is the master or transaction form for which the excel template has to be downloaded. 
 Nested Objects: Some forms which have to be imported have a lot of data, and have multiple excel worksheets in one excel template. These multiple worksheets normally correspond to tabs of the entry interface. Example, Account Head Import will have the worksheets for Ledger, Ledger Address, Ledger Communication, Ledger Contact, Bank Details, etc. 
 All these worksheets are linked to each other through a common field called Link Ref Code . The same value of this field in each row has to be entered under ImportLinkRefCode in the nested worksheets. In the Ledger worksheet Link Ref Code ‘1’ has details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ has details of Amit Kumar Pal. In the Ledger Address worksheet, ImportLinkRefCode ‘1’ will contain address details of Amar Singh, Link Ref Code ‘2’ will contain address details of Amit Kumar Pal. The value given to the Link Ref Code and ImportLinkRefCode has to be the same so that data in the different worksheets can be associated with each other. 
 Download template : Download the template by clicking the Download button. An excel file will be downloaded on your local computer. Open the excel sheet. Enter the data in the excel sheet. 
 About the Excel Template 
 There may be one or more worksheets in which data has to or can be entered. Click on the different worksheets to enter data in them. Remember to use the same identifying value in all worksheets so that data between the different worksheets can be linked to each other. In case there is no data to be filled in the nested worksheets, leave it blank. Do not fill only the ImportLinkRefCode if no other data is available for entry in that sheet. In case there is a row in the main sheet but there is no associated data for that row in the linked sheets, skip that row number in the linked sheet. 
 Each excel template has an Info worksheet which will guide the user about the properties of the fields. 
 Sheet Name : Worksheet names are listed here. 
 Column Names : Fields available in all associated worksheets are listed here. Data has to be entered as rows, fields are the columns. 
 Properties : Fields can have the following properties 
 Is required: True - this is a mandatory field, has to be entered. 
 Is required: False - this is an optional field. 
 Max length: The maximum number of characters which can be entered in that field. 
 The following points have to be kept in mind while filling data in the prescribed excel sheet 
 Do not remove any columns or worksheets , even if there is no data to be entered in them. Format must be as per the original excel template downloaded. 
 Do not change any names, settings, alignment, formatting of fields, worksheet, or files . 
 Remove any hyperlinks from the data fields . Example Email. 
 Try to import records into batches of 100, 200 or 500 rows at a time. Import can be run multiple times. Data will keep on getting added in Farvision. 
 Fill all mandatory fields 
 Enter data in ImportLinkRefCode if data is there in the associated worksheets 
 Do not enter blank rows , especially at the end of the excel sheet 
 Wherever applicable, Debit and Credit amounts should tally . 
 Spelling of account heads, parent account, items, etc should be correct, i.e. match with the masters in Farvision 
 Wherever applicable, data in related sheets should tally with the data in the main sheet . Example, Receipt/Payment or Journals, the Adjustment Info amount for each party should tally with the amount in Ledger details for the same party. 
 Some tips 
 Clear cache and clear history of the browser, in case of unknown error 
 UPLOAD TEMPLATE 
 Upload the filled out excel Template to start the data uploading process. 
 Select File : Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. 
 The template can be dragged and dropped or the same can be selected from its location. Click on the Drop files to upload panel. Select the file in which data has been entered and has to be uploaded. Click on the Upload button. Once the template has been uploaded, it will show the message Uploaded Successfully. Click on Next button to go to the data validation step. VALIDATE DATA Once the filled up excel has been uploaded, the data has to be validated from the template and click on Next 
 Process Queue : Click on the box so that the validation process can be routed through the Queue Management console. If the data volume is large, it is important to queue this process else the server will become very slow. 
 Validate Data : Click on the Start Validation button to start the validation process. 
 Status : While the data validation is ongoing, a status bar will show Validating Data, Please Wait. If the data validation is successful, it will show the status as Success. If data is not correct and has failed the validation process, it will show Error Found. 
 Result : In case the status is not successful, the reasons why validation has failed will be provided in this Excel file which can be downloaded. The file will have both data which has a problem and data which is correct. The data where there is a problem is highlighted in yellow. The problems with the data will be displayed in the Import Remarks column. In this example, HSN Id does not exist for Construction service in HSN Master. 
 In this example, Relationship should have Son or Wife, and the name Rakesh Kumar and Mahaveer Singh should have been entered in Relative Name respectively. 
 In this example, Postal code is a mandatory field that can’t be blank. 
 The validation routine has to be run repeatedly till there are no errors left. 
 Click on the Next button to go to the Import Data tab. 
 IMPORT DATA 
 Click on Start Import to start importing data from filled up excel template file into Farvision. On successful import, it will show the status as Success. Click on the Finish button. Data which has been imported can be checked in the respective Advanced Search for the transaction or master forms. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

text:
Back date entry blocking for stock updating 
 Farvision r2 What's New" />

 entry blocking for stock updating

 Unit 
 of Measurement 
 Users can create custom units of measurement 
 based on their specific needs. This means that users can define and utilise 
 unconventional units, such as "Number," "Bag," "Square 
 Feet," and more, according to their requirements. 
 Benefits 
 This feature lets users adjust the measurement 
 system to fit what they need. This flexibility ensures that the system 
 can correctly measure different types of things, making the measurements 
 more accurate and relevant. 
 Use Case 
 In the real estate industry, this feature 
 is used to define unique units of measurement. For example, the user could 
 use the "Number" unit for counting individual items, and "Square 
 Feet" for measuring floor space. By customising these units, the 
 system can effectively manage inventory and allocate space with greater 
 accuracy and efficiency. 
 It 
 is highly recommended that UOM as per govt. of India is used. This will 
 help in proper generation of e-invoices and GST returns. If UOMs which

 rejected. Approved UOMs can be downloaded from https://einvoice1.gst.gov.in/others/mastercodes . UOMs are called Unique Quantity 
 Code (UQC) by the govt.

 for "Kilogram"

title: Item Group Wise Account Head Tag
text:
Item Group Wise Account Head Tagging 
 Help > Setup > Item" />
 Tutorial: Account Head Group Tagging 
 Item Group 
 Wise Account Head Tagging 
 Account group head tagging interface is used to 
 tag the item group with the account head against which the purchase is 
 to be done. 
 Benefits 
 This interface is useful for streamlining 
 and organising the purchasing process. By tagging the item group with 
 the account head, it ensures that purchases are made efficiently and accurately, 
 while also providing a clear trail of accountability. 
 Account heads can be changed from this 
 section, if needed. 
 Use Case 
 In the real estate industry, a property 
 development company is managing multiple construction projects simultaneously. 
 Each project requires various materials. By using this interface interface, 
 the company can effectively tag specific item groups with the relevant 
 account heads. 
 For example, when the construction team 
 needs to purchase materials they can easily identify the account head 
 against which the purchase should be recorded. 
 Steps to Perform Item Group Wise Account Head Tagging 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Material> Setup> 
 Item> Item Group Wise Account Head Tagging. The following screen 
 will appear. 
 2. 2. 
 Choose the Item Group 
 for whom the account head needs to be changed. Once selected, click on 
 the Edit 
 option from th e drop-down list. 
 P.S: The account head is already tagged 
 as Purchase A/C by default. If the user wants to make any changes to the 
 account head, it can be done from this interface. 
 3. The following window will open from 
 where the preferred Account Head can be chosen. 
 Item Group : Auto-populated from 
 Item Group master. 
 Item Type : Auto-populated from 
 Item Group master. 
 Account Head : Choose the preferred 
 Account Head. 
 Closing Stock P&L: Only applicable for P&L Based Item 
 Type. Not applicable for other Item Types. If the user inserts a value 
 into this field, it will not have any effect. 
 Closing Stock BS: Only applicable for P&L Based Item Type. Not 
 applicable for other Item Types. If the user inserts a value into this 
 field, it will not have any effect. 
 3. 4. Click on Save to save 
 the entry. Once done, the Account Head will 
 be updated as follows. 
 Tutorial: 
 Account Head Group Tagging 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Item Master
text:
Item Master 
 Help > Setup > Item" />
 Tutorial: Creating Item Master 
 Item 
 Master 
 ‘Item Master’ interface will facilitate user 
 to set the Item code along with its Item Group and Type of item. 
 Benefit 
 This interface offers a streamlined 
 approach to managing property-related inventory and supplies, providing 
 real estate professionals with a centralised system to assign item codes, 
 item groups, and types of items. 
 Use Case 
 In 
 a real estate firm, the property management department is responsible 
 for maintaining and replenishing various types of inventories (e.g. construction 
 material, office equipment, fixed assets), for multiple properties. By 
 utilising this interface, the department can easily set and categorise 
 item codes, assign them to specific item groups and specify the type of 
 each item. 
 Main Info 
 Code : Specify the Item Code like "IM0001" 
 Description : Enter 
 the description of the item (Mandatory) as "Cement ACC" 
 Stock UOM : Unit of measurement 
 for stock material is to be entered here (Mandatory) 
 Alternate Description : Provide 
 alternate description if any 
 Detail Description : Enter 
 detail description of the material like "Cement for plastering" 
 Group Name : Select 
 the item group. The item that has been specified in the ‘Item Description’ 
 field belongs to this item group (Mandatory) as "Cement". 
 Item Type : As soon as user 
 selects the Item Group, the type of item will automatically come into 
 view in this field. 
 Valuation : Select the item valuation type. 
 The valuation method differs depending upon the chosen type of item. Options 
 include ‘Average’ and ‘FIFO’. It is to be noted that if the type of item 
 is ‘Raw Material’, then the valuation process will be ‘Average’. 
 Tolerance For PO : Set 
 the percentage of Purchase Order tolerance. Tolerance refers to the allowable 
 limit to make a purchase order. 
 Lead Time (Days) : Enter 
 number of days considered as lead time for supplying the item. 
 Batch 
 Wise : This check box is for yes or no type. If user wants the item 
 to be batch wise, then check else do not check. 
 Discontinue : 
 This field is also for yes or no type. If user wants to discontinue the 
 item, then check else do not check. 
 UOM 
 Select 
 the ‘ UOM ’ tab to set item’s ‘Unit of Measurement’. As per the requirement, 
 user can set multiple UOMs (Unit of Measurement) against a single item. 
 Besides setting the UOM, user will also be able to define Stock UOM, Receive 
 UOM, Issue UOM, Factor and Conversion Ratio. 
 Add New 
 Row 
 Click 
 ‘Add New Row’ to define new UOM 
 UOM : Select 
 unit of measurement 
 Conversion Factor : Select 
 conversion factor. For example ‘/’ or ‘*’ (Division or multiplication) 
 Conversion Ratio : Enter 
 conversion ratio 
 Receive UOM : Check to enable receiving UOM 
 Issue UOM : Check to enable issuing UOM 
 For example, 
 the ‘Exact Conversion’ is the conventional process, where 1kg always equals 
 to 1000 gms (or 1 km = 1000 meter), whereas, the ‘Inexact Conversion’ 
 is the calculation process, where 1kg can be equal to 10 Box or 11 Box 
 or 9 Box. 
 Click ‘Finish’ 
 Change History 
 Clicking on this tab will show history of any changes 
 done with information of user, modification date and action.

 master Import 
 Item master Auto code setup:

 group creation (whenever creating an item group, group code can’t have 
 code more than 2 characters, as Item master auto code setup is based on 
 the Item group code).

 master no item code was mentioned. 
 Item has been saved with Auto code 
 SC-Top 
 group code

 Numbering 
 Scenario2: Item creation under sub 
 group 
 Auto numbering 
 FACAPC0001

 digits Top group code 
 CA-Two 
 digits Sub group code 
 PC- 
 Two digits sub sub group code 
 0001-Auto 
 numbering 
 Additional Features: 
 1. Creator id column in Item 
 Master export to excel: After clicking on the Item master excel output, 
 new columns creator id now has been added. 
 2. Discontinued (Yes\No) status 
 option in Item Master advance search: Now 
 in Item master advanced search, Item discontinued status can be checked. 
 3. Document print format: User can now be able to print Item master 
 print format. To activate this option user requires to run sync 
 & print option access for the Item master. 
 Please click on advance search 
 option and select an item and click the print option from toolbar 
 Tutorial: Creating Item Master

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

 Item Group

 some item groups in order to grouping some items which are either made

 type determine the posting/accounting methodology of the item will create

 Cost Center 
 Master 
 Cost Centres can be 
 used in 
 accounts or inventory related entries. Accounts related cost centres help in monitoring notional costs for

 to n-level of cost centres. Cost centre s 
 are a component or element of Dimensions which are globally available 
 in Farvision. 
 Receipt/Payment, 
 journal vouchers and non-store purchases allow for tagging of cost centres 
 for accounting expenses. Example, Rs 10000 are Telephone expenses. Telephone 
 expenses is the expense account head which will be debited. The expense 
 can be further split between different cost centres like departments, 
 users, regions, etc. These cost centre do not have any accounting impact. 
 They are a reporting mechanism only. 
 Farvision 
 engineer module provides for very exhaustive tracking of costs. In case 
 engineering module is not being used, material costs can be monitored 
 through inventory cost centres also. Cost of material being issued / consumed 
 (through Issue) can be assigned to cost centres like Head Office, Blocks 
 or Towers, Repair accounts as your cost centre groups and cost centres 
 have been created. 
 Also 
 if material is given to other projects on loan and we do not want to impact 
 books of accounts, we can use issue or transfer material and tag the other 
 BU as a cost centre. This is used in case Inter Location stock transfer 
 is not going to be used.

 Example name of mobile numbers, name of persons, regions, departments,

 Inventory posting head has to be defined for cost centres here. The posting 
 account head into which cost centre expenses will be posted during the

text:
Store Requisition Revision 
 Help > Requisition" />
 Tutorial: 
 Creating Store Requisition Revision 
 Store Requisition 
 Revision 
 ‘Store 
 Requisition Revision’ interface is used to make revision of item requisition 
 entry for stores. 
 Benefit of Store Requisition Revision 
 The benefit of store requisition 
 revision is that it helps change the current requisition request. 
 Note: If 100% requisition quantity is 
 utilised, then an amendment or revision is not possible because the requirements 
 are already fulfilled. 
 Use Case Scenario 
 This interface has two applicable use 
 case scenarios: 
 1. For Amendment : This interface 
 is utilised when there is a need for adjustments beyond the initially 
 mentioned quantity for a project. Whether it's an increase or decrease 
 in the originally requested amount, it is essential to ensure that the 
 requisition aligns with the updated project requirements. 
 2. For Short close : This interface 
 is used to close the requisition for the unused materials. 
 Scenario 
 1: Amendment (click to learn the steps) 
 In a construction project, initially, 
 100 bags of cement are requisitioned. As the project progresses, the on-site 
 team realises that an additional 50 bags of cement are needed to complete 
 the work. This situation calls for the use of the interface for revision, 
 where the Requisition type is set as an amendment to add the extra 50 
 bags of cement to the existing requisition. 
 On the other hand, suppose 100 bags 
 of cement were initially requested. As work progresses, it becomes clear 
 that only 60 bags of cement are needed to complete the project. In this 
 case, the interface for amendment is used to revise the requisition, reflecting 
 the reduced quantity of 40 bags of cement, which aligns with the actual 
 requirement. 
 Scenario 2: 
 Short Close (click to learn the steps) 
 In a real estate construction 
 project, short close helps adjust excess materials like cement bags, bricks, 
 steel, sand, and metal that were initially requested but not fully used. 
 For example, if 100 units of each item were requested but only 80 units 
 of each will be used, through this interface, the user can close the unused 
 20 units of each material, all at once.

title: Bulk Indent Short Close
text:
Bulk Indent Short Close 
 Help > Requisition" />
 Bulk 
 Indent Short Close 
 This 
 interface is used to make bulk indent short close. 
 B enefits of Bulk Indent Short 
 Close 
 By utilising the interface designed 
 for bulk indent short close, users can now streamline the process of closing 
 multiple indents simultaneously. It is particularly beneficial for developers 
 who deal with multiple indents and need to execute 'short close' transactions 
 quickly to maintain profitability and cash flow. 
 Use Case Scenario 
 Managing multiple 
 indents for project materials is crucial. However, changing project requirements 
 often render some indents which are not required, leading to surplus inventory. 
 The introduction 
 of a bulk indent short close interface enables the store in-charge to 
 identify and close multiple indents in one go, saving time and reducing 
 errors. 
 Steps to Perform Bulk Indent Short Close 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Material> Requisition> 
 Bulk Indent Short Close. The following screen will be visible. 
 1. 2. 
 Fill in the fields as required: 
 Business 
 Unit: Choose the preferred 
 BU from the list. 
 As on Date: 
 This denotes the pending indents from 
 the selected date. 
 Days: I f 
 data exists in this field, the displayed indents will fall within the 
 range from the ‘From Date’ to the ‘As on Date’. For instance, if the ‘As 
 on Date’ is set to the 7th of any given month, and the ‘Days’ field contains

 to the 7th of that particular month.

RFQ Generation

 RFQ Generation 
 RFQ generation involves creating and 
 issuing requests for quotation to potential suppliers or vendors in response 
 to specific material requirements. In this context, the RFQ is generated 
 against all the indents created, indicating that the RFQs are being issued 
 to multiple suppliers or vendors to gather competitive quotations for 
 the items or services requested. 
 User 
 can generate the RFQ based on the Tender. User can always generate RFQ 
 at the current date. 
 Benefits of RFQ Generation 
 Generating requests for quotations (RFQs) 
 against all the indents—indicating the creation of RFQs for every material 
 requirement—offers numerous advantages. 
 Issuing RFQs against all indents enables 
 companies to engage with a diverse range of suppliers, fostering healthy 
 competition and potentially uncovering new, reliable partners. This process 
 also facilitates well-informed decision-making by gathering a variety 
 of quotations, allowing organisations to consider factors such as price, 
 quality, and supplier credibility.

 Tutorial: Creating Indent Revision 
 Indent 
 Revision 
 Indent revision is 
 required to carry out any alteration or cancellation to the original indent. 
 Through Indent Revision, all the changes or alteration against a particular 
 indent can be tracked. 
 Benefits of Indent Revision 
 Using indent revision can offer the 
 significant benefit of maintaining a clear and transparent record of all 
 alterations made to the original indent. By tracking changes made to the 
 indent, all parties can stay informed and updated on modifications, helping 
 to streamline the overall process and maintain accuracy in documentation. 
 Use Case Scenario 
 This 
 interface has two applicable use case scenarios: 
 1. 
 For Amendment : This interface is utilised when there is a need 
 for adjustments beyond the initially mentioned quantity for a project. 
 Whether it's an increase or decrease in the original indent, it is essential 
 to ensure that the indent aligns with the updated project requirements. 
 2. For Short close : This interface is used 
 to close the indent for the unused materials. 
 Scenario 1: 
 Amendment 
 In 
 a construction project, initially, 100 bags of cement are set for indent. 
 As the project progresses, the on-site team realises that an additional 
 50 bags of cement are needed to complete the work. This situation calls 
 for the use of the interface for revision, where the Amendment type is 
 set as an amendment to add the extra 50 bags of cement to the existing 
 indent. 
 On 
 the other hand, suppose 100 bags of cement were initially requested. As 
 work progresses, it becomes clear that only 60 bags of cement are needed 
 to complete the project. In this case, the interface for amendment is 
 used to revise the indent, reflecting the reduced quantity of 40 bags 
 of cement, which aligns with the actual requirement. 
 Scenario 
 2: Short Close 
 In a real estate construction project, short close 
 helps adjust excess materials like cement bags, bricks, steel, sand, and 
 metal that were put in the indent but not fully used. For example, if 
 100 units of each item were set in the indent but only 80 units of each 
 will be used, through this interface, the user can close the unused 20 
 units of each material, all at once.

 Amendment in this field.

title: Price Comparison
text:
Price Comparison 
 Help > Vendor Management" />
 Price Comparison 
 The price comparison 
 interface helps facilitate vendor management by enabling businesses to 
 efficiently compare and analyse supplier prices. This interface is integrated 
 within the procurement and supply chain functionalities, allowing for 
 seamless retrieval and comparison of vendor pricing data for various products 
 and services. 
 Benefits of Price Comparison Interface 
 The incorporation 
 of such an interface offers numerous benefits, including significant cost 
 savings through informed vendor selection, enhanced efficiency by automating 
 the comparison process, and the ability to make data-driven purchasing 
 decisions. Additionally, it provides a solid foundation for vendor negotiations 
 and equips businesses with valuable market intelligence to maintain competitiveness. 
 Use Case Scenario 
 Consider a company has received various 
 quotations from multiple suppliers for the materials it needs. To determine 
 the most advantageous deal, the company uses a Price Comparison interface. 
 This interface displays a grid with all the supplier quotes side by side, 
 enabling the user to quickly assess which supplier offers the best terms. 
 The subsequent sections of the document 
 will guide the user on how to update their supplier choice using the interface. 
 Steps to Perform Price Comparison 
 1. 1. 
 Navigate to Material> 
 Vendor Management> Price Comparison. The following screen will 
 be displayed. 
 2. Choose the Business Unit and PCC 
 No. as applicable. The following grid will populate. 
 From the above screen, there are two 
 suppliers from which the same materials’ quotation can be seen. 
 The one marked in green is suggested 
 by the system. 
 The user can make the decision on which 
 supplier to go for. 
 Also, users can also download the related 
 report in an excel format. 
 3. Click on the icon in the following 
 screen after which the excel sheet will be downloaded. 
 The downloaded excel report can be seen 
 as follows. 
 Now, if the user wants to change the 
 preferred supplier from the one already displayed in green to the other 
 one, there is an option to do so. 
 4. Click on the hamburger menu in the 
 top-right corner of the screen where the option to Update Supplier is 
 available. 
 5. 
 Choose the preferred supplier 
 from the drop-down list and input any reason for the change. Click on 
 Save once done. 
 The following screen is now visible 
 with the updated supplier preference. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Note For Approval
text:
Note For Approval 
 Help > Procurement" />
 Note For 
 Approval 
 The 
 Note for Approval is a structured document or form that outlines 
 specific parameters or requests requiring approval from the management. 
 This note typically includes details such as payment terms, final negotiations, 
 retention money, vendor scope, and other critical aspects of a business 
 transaction or decision. It serves as a formal communication tool to seek 
 authorisation or sign-off from relevant management personnel before proceeding 
 with any work order. 
 What Is the Benefit of Note for Approval? 
 One 
 of the significant advantages of creating a Note for Approval is 
 that it helps ensure proper control over key business decisions and processes. 
 By explicitly documenting and seeking approval for various parameters, 
 organisations can enforce accountability, prevent unauthorised actions, 
 and reduce risks associated with unchecked operations. 
 Use Case 
 Consider a company in the process of 
 finalising a contract with a supplier for the supply of essential materials 
 required for their upcoming project. Before officially committing to the 
 agreement, the procurement team has created a Note for Approval to ensure 
 all critical aspects are reviewed and approved by the management team. 
 Steps to Create 
 Note for Approval 
 1. 1. Navigate 
 to Material> Procurement> Note for Approval. The following 
 window can be seen. 
 2. Fill 
 in the mandatory fields such as Business Unit, Financial Year, Document 
 Type, and Supplier . For the other fields, fill the ones applicable 
 for the project. After filling in the necessary field, the following window 
 can be seen. 
 Business 
 Unit : Choose the applicable Business Unit. 
 Financial 
 Year : By default, current financial year will be auto-populated otherwise 
 it can be changed according to the user requirement. 
 Document Type: A 
 document is categorised based on its purpose or function, such as purchase 
 order or work order. 
 Document 
 Date: I t is the date when a specific document is created or issued. 
 Document 
 No : A unique identifier assigned to a specific document for tracking 
 and reference purposes. This is also auto-populated. 
 Supplier : 
 The entity or organisation from which the services are to be procured. 
 Original/Amendment : 
 If the WO is new, choose the Original option. If it is selected as amendment, 
 after entering the Previous Contract Amount and the Amendment Value, it 
 gets tagged in WO Amendment under Amendment module. 
 Previous 
 Contract Details : Information about the previous agreement or contract, 
 including relevant terms and conditions. 
 Previous Contract Amount: The monetary value associated with the previous 
 contract. 
 Proposed Order Value: The 
 total amount proposed for the order (applicable only if the work order 
 is new). 
 Amendment 
 Value : In case of amendment work order, this value is applicable. 
 Subject : 
 A brief description or title of the document, summarizing its content. 
 Scope 
 of Work : The tasks, activities, and deliverables included in the project 
 or contract. 
 Technical 
 Specification : Detailed descriptions of the technical requirements, 
 standards, and features related to the project or procurement. 
 Payment 
 Terms : The agreed-upon conditions and schedule for making payments 
 on the contract or order. 
 Final 
 Negotiation : The last stage of discussions and agreements before finalizing 
 the terms of the contract or order. 
 Retention 
 Money : A portion of the payment was withheld to ensure the fulfillment 
 of contractual obligations, often released after the completion of the 
 contract. 
 Billing 
 Procedure : This is the method and process for generating and submitting 
 invoices for the goods or services provided. 
 Our Scope: The 
 specific areas of responsibility or deliverables assigned to the organisation 
 issuing the document. 
 Vendor 
 Scope : The specific areas of responsibility or deliverables assigned 
 to the vendor or supplier. 
 Mode 
 of Measurement : The method or criteria used to quantify or measure 
 the work or services provided. 
 Workmen 
 Compensation Policy : The insurance policy providing coverage for work-related 
 injuries or illnesses suffered by employees. 
 PF 
 No./ESIC : Provident Fund (PF) Number and Employee State Insurance 
 Corporation (ESIC) details, pertaining to social security measures for 
 employees. 
 Labour 
 License : The official authorisation or permit required for engaging 
 in labour for specific activities. 
 CAR 
 Policy/Third Party (Developers Scope) : Contingent Auto Repair (CAR) 
 Policy or insurance coverage for damages to third-party property caused 
 during project execution. 
 Warranty/Guarantee : 
 The assurance provided by the supplier regarding the quality and performance 
 of goods or services, often including specified warranty periods. 
 Safety 
 Parameters : The defined measures and standards for ensuring safety 
 and minimizing risks during project execution. 
 Drawing No.: The 
 unique identifier assigned to technical or engineering drawings related 
 to the project or contract. 
 Remarks : 
 Additional comments, notes, or observations relevant to the document or 
 its contents. 
 3. 
 Click on Submit once done. 
 4. Now, 
 click on the Advanced Search Icon on the top-right corner of the screen. 
 From there the new entry made is visible. 
 Now, navigate to Material> Procurement> Purchase 
 Order. There is an option to tag this newly created Note for Approval 
 for that specific BU under the Creating Purchase Order tab . 
 This implies that after obtaining the Note for Approval, it can be mapped 
 against the Purchase Order. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Vehicle In/Out
text:
Vehicle In/Out 
 Help > Receiving" />
 Vehicle 
 In/Out 
 The interface is designed to capture 
 vehicle movement details along with measurements and billing information, 
 whether the vehicle is arriving with loaded material or departing to another 
 location. The system supports weighbridge integration for vehicles, whether 
 they are loaded or empty. 
 If weighbridge integration is enabled, 
 the material quantity is automatically captured from the weighbridge software 
 when the "Get Weight" button is clicked. For instance, Aerosol 
 IO provides an integration API with weighbridges and Farvision. 
 In some cases, camera integration with 
 the weighbridge is also implemented (e.g., Wright weighbridges). This 
 allows the capture of photos or videos along with the weight data, which 
 can be viewed as attachments in Farvision and through the FV Store 
 mobile app. 
 For certain weighbridges, complete integration 
 is in place. This means that when a transaction is recorded in the weighbridge 
 software, a corresponding document is automatically created in Farvision. 
 Without 
 Weighbridge Integration 
 With Weighbridge 
 Integration 
 Main Info 
 Business Unit: Select the 
 business unit. 
 Financial year: Current 
 financial year is displayed by default, can be changed if required. 
 Document Type: Select whether 
 a vehicle is coming in or going out. 
 i) Vehicle 
 Movement (In)(MID): Normally, inward movement is with goods coming 
 in. 
 ii) Vehicle 
 Movement (Out)(GP): Vehicles out is for 
 a. empty 
 vehicle weighment after unloading the material 
 or 
 b. goods 
 going outside the business unit premises for sales, transfer, issue, purchase 
 return. More details of goods out is described in Against field below.

 displayed by default which can be changed. 
 Document No : The Vehicle 
 In/Out document number generated and populated automatically after saving 
 the entry. 
 Against Doc type : Only 
 for outward movement of vehicles, does against document type have to be 
 selected. A vehicle can move out either empty or with goods. For an empty 
 vehicle, select Material Inward. For a vehicle going out with goods choose 
 from any of the other options, except Material Inward. 
 Material Inward 
 - for empty vehicles (after unloading goods) 
 Purchase Debit 
 Note - for Purchase return against purchase debit note 
 Inter Location 
 Transfer - for Stock transfer to other Business Unit 
 Transfer - for 
 to warehouse or godown within same Business Unit 
 Issue - for Issue 
 to sub contractor, employee, vendor for any purpose like repairing, or 
 being given. 
 Sale Bill - for 
 sale (through Sale bill) to a customer or business unit 
 Select Document : 
 Document list will be displayed as per the document type selected in Against 
 field above. Example, if Material Inward is selected, select the MID number 
 against which the goods had come in. The Vehicle number will get automatically 
 populated. Another example, if goods are being sold, Sales Bill will be 
 displayed so that the document against which goods are moving out can 
 be tagged. 
 Example of Material Inward documents available 
 for selection for vehicle out (for unloaded vehicle) 
 Example of Stock transfer documents available 
 for selection for vehicle out, which are carrying goods against this document.

 number.

 show current time. Change the time by using clock popup. 
 Height: Enter the Vehicle 
 height. 
 Width: Enter the vehicle 
 width. 
 Length: Enter the vehicle 
 length. 
 Supplier: Choose the supplier 
 name, on behalf of which the vehicle is carrying goods in. This option 
 is only available for vehicle movement in. 
 Select Order: Tag the purchase 
 order against the entry will be made. This option is only available for 
 vehicle movement in. 
 Supplier ref no: Enter the 
 supplier reference number through which goods are coming in, i.e. the 
 supplier’s challan number. 
 Supplier ref date: Enter 
 the date of suppliers challan or reference number. 
 Quantity: Enter the material 
 quantity. In case of integration with a weighbridge, this will be fetched 
 by pressing the Get Weight button. 
 Get Weight : In case any 
 weighbridge is integrated, click on this button to get weight. Normally, 
 the vehicle will be on the weighbridge for the weight to be automatically 
 captured from the weighbridge. 
 Remarks: Enter remarks on 
 vehicle In/Out if any. 
 Attachment 
 In 
 case weighbridge has a camera, the photographs, video will automatically 
 get captured in Farvision. The photographs for each entry can be viewed 
 here. 
 Video 
 of vehicle movement, order copy, invoice copy against which goods are 
 supplied, party challan (transporter road transport document), vehicle 
 registration and driver’s license copy have been attached. 
 Some 
 more examples of attachments captured from weighbridges

title: Quality Control Console
text:
Quality Control Console 
 Help > Quality Control" />
 Quality 
 Control Console 
 What is the Quality Control Console? 
 The Quality Control Console is an interface 
 designed to ensure that various parameters of the materials meet predefined 
 standards. These quality parameters could include standard structural 
 specifications, safety features, compliance with local regulations, and 
 overall quality of the material. 
 The console allows users to input, monitor, and evaluate these parameters 
 to maintain high standards in real estate projects. 
 What is the Importance of Quality Control Console? 
 The Quality Control Console is crucial 
 for several reasons. Firstly, it maintains the quality of construction 
 by monitoring various parameters, leading to higher customer satisfaction. 
 Additionally, it aids in risk management by identifying potential issues 
 early in the construction process, allowing for timely interventions and 
 reducing the risk of costly repairs later. Lastly, it streamlines the 
 quality control process, making it easier and faster to conduct inspections 
 and generate reports. 
 When is the Quality Control Console Used? 
 The Quality Control Console is used 
 during the procurement of materials, with regular checks conducted to 
 ensure ongoing compliance and quality. 
 Steps to Use Quality Control Console 
 Navigate to Material> Quality Control> 
 Quality Control Console. 
 The following screen can be seen. 
 Business Unit : Choose the preferred 
 Business Unit. 
 Date From : Choose the date from 
 which the Quality Control will begin. 
 Date To : Choose the date until 
 which the Quality Control will be conducted. 
 Quality Inspection For: Under this field, there are multiple 
 options. Choose the preferred one. The options are as follows: 
 Goods Received From Supplier: This option 
 is selected when the quality inspection is being conducted on goods 
 that have been received directly from a supplier. 
 Goods Received From Contractor Receivable: 
 This option is used when the quality inspection is for goods received 
 from a contractor that are receivable, meaning they are expected to 
 be returned or accounted for. 
 Goods Received From Contractor Non Receivable: 
 This option is selected when the quality inspection is for goods received 
 from a contractor that are non-receivable, meaning they are not expected 
 to be returned. 
 Show Details For: Under this field, 
 there are multiple options which will be explained further in this guide. 
 The 
 options are as follows: 
 Pending For Sending To Quality Control: 
 This option 
 is selected when you want to view details of items that are awaiting 
 dispatch to the Quality Control department for inspection. 
 Pending For Laboratory: This option is used 
 to view details of items that are pending laboratory testing. 
 Complete Inspection: This option is selected 
 to view details of items that have completed the quality inspection 
 process. 
 All : This 
 option is used to view details of all items, regardless of their inspection 
 status. 
 After filling in the above details, 
 choose either of the options from Show Details For. 
 Pending For Sending To Quality Control 
 Click on the search icon to populate 
 all the Documents under Pending For Sending To Quality Control. 
 Once done, the 
 screen would look similar to the following. 
 Click on any 
 document from the list upon which the following screen can be seen. 
 Item Description : Auto populated. 
 Sample Quantity Sent For Inspection : 
 The amount of material sent for quality testing. 
 Sample No : A unique identifier 
 assigned to the sample being inspected (non-mandatory field). 
 Any Specific Instruction to be given 
 with Ref. To BOQ: Special 
 instructions related to the Bill of Quantities (BOQ) for the inspection 
 process (non-mandatory field). 
 Generate Bar Code: Click on the Generate button to generate 
 a unique barcode. 
 Once the above details are filled, the 
 screen would look similar to the following. 
 Click on Save once done. The 
 quantity which is to be sent for a sample will be processed and will now 
 be available in the list of pending documents. 
 A ‘Saved Successfully’ message will 
 appear on the screen. 
 Pending For Laboratory 
 Once the above document is successfully 
 saved, click on the search icon 
 to populate all the Documents for Pending For Laboratory. 
 The following screen should be visible. 
 Click on the grid upon which the following 
 screen will open. 
 The detail about this screen is explained 
 in Rejected 
 from Laboratory

 Click on the search icon to populate 
 all the Documents for Complete Inspection. 
 The screen should 
 look similar to the following.

 all the Documents for Quantity Control. 
 The green ones denote the Approved Documents.

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Rejected From Laboratory
text:
Rejected From Laboratory 
 Help > Quality Control" />
 Rejected 
 From Laboratory 
 What is the "Rejected From Laboratory" 
 Interface? 
 The ‘Rejected 
 From Laboratory’ interface is an essential part of the Material Module 
 within a procurement system. It deals with instances where materials undergo 
 quality inspections but fail to meet the required standards. When materials 
 are marked as "failed" in the Quality Inspection Status interface, 
 they are automatically flagged and transferred to this interface. 
 Why is the Interface Important? 
 The purpose 
 of this interface is to ensure the proper handling of materials that do 
 not meet quality expectations. 
 When is the Interface Activated? 
 This interface 
 is triggered whenever a material fails to pass the quality inspection 
 process. This typically occurs after the material is received and undergoes 
 a review against predefined quality parameters. If the material does not 
 meet the necessary standards, it is marked as "failed" in the 
 Quality Inspection Status interface. 
 Steps to Use Rejected From Laboratory Interface 
 Navigate 
 to Material> Quality Control> Rejected From Laboratory. 
 If any document does not pass the Quality 
 Parameters, the same will populate here. 
 Let’s 
 take an example where the user has selected the Fail option in one of 
 the materials in Quality 
 Inspection Status interface. 
 Enter the observed value as 
 needed. 
 The Failed document will populate 
 here in the main screen of the Rejected From Laboratory interface. 
 Click on the grid to open the 
 following screen. 
 Here the user can view the Quality Parameter 
 checklist under the condition ‘Fail’. 
 There are multiple options under Remarks 
 for Approvers. 
 Choose the appropriate one along with 
 any comments and click Save. 
 If 
 the material is Passed Under Deviation, check the box. 
 Once 
 you click on Save, the item of material would not appear in this interface 
 anymore. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Quality Inspection Status
text:
Quality Inspection Status 
 Help > Quality Control" />
 Quality 
 Inspection Status 
 What is Quality Inspection Status? 
 Quality Inspection Status refers to 
 the current state or progress of quality inspections conducted on materials 
 for a business unit. This status provides the data, where each item stands 
 in the quality control process, indicating whether it is pending inspection, 
 currently under inspection, or has completed inspection. 
 Why is Quality Inspection Status Important? 
 The Quality Inspection Status is vital 
 because it provides transparency by offering clear and real-time information 
 about the quality inspection process, ensuring that all stakeholders are 
 informed about the current status of inspections. 
 When is Quality Inspection Status Used? 
 Quality Inspection Status is used during 
 procurement of materials. It tracks the status of quality inspections 
 for materials received from suppliers and contractors before they are 
 used in construction. 
 Steps to Use Quality Inspection Status 
 Navigate to Material> Quality Control> 
 Quality Inspection Status. 
 The following screen will be visible. 
 Inspection Status: Under this field, 
 there are 3 options. 
 Pending : 
 Items that are awaiting quality inspection. 
 Complete : 
 Items that have finished the quality inspection process. 
 All : 
 Includes all items, regardless of their inspection status. 
 Date From: The date from which the Quality 
 Inspection Status will be conducted. 
 Date To: The date until which the Quality 
 Inspection Status will be conducted. 
 Click on the grid to open the following 
 screen. 
 Enter the Observed Value for each of 
 the Quality Parameters. 
 Check the Passed box if the material 
 passes the Quality Inspection. 
 If not, check the Failed box. 
 Enter any Remarks for QC, if applicable. 
 Once done, click on Save. An Updated Successfully message will appear on the screen. 
 Once the inspection is passed, the grid 
 will turn green, indicating that it has been approved by the respective 
 user. 
 Completed 
 All the Completed documents can be seen 
 in this window within the designated timeframe. 
 All 
 All documents can be seen in this window 
 within the designated timeframe. 
 Attachment 
 User 
 can send Quality Control email with attachment. 
 Quality 
 Control Report 
 Quality 
 Control Email with body can be generated in Quality Inspection Status at the time of QC sample accepted 
 or Rejected. 
 a) 
 As per the default option selected in document design the sample QC report 
 print will be attached in the mail body. 
 b) 
 Mail will generated during saving, after QC sample is Accepted or Rejected. 
 Following 
 steps are required to send Quality Control Email: 
 Step1 : Create Email template for 
 the Entry Type 'Quality Inspection' as shown below through Administration > 
 Communicator > Email Template 
 Step2 : Create Communication Rule 
 on update mode as shown below through Administration 
 > Communicator > Communication Rule 
 Click 
 on 'Template Mapping' and select the Template created in step1. Save to 
 set the communication rule. 
 Step3 : 
 Now in 'Quality Inspection Status', 
 in 'Quality Inspection' popup, 
 the m ail will 
 be sent after clicking the save button as shown below 
 Sample Mail Body

 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Issue Return
text:
Issue Return

 Tutorial: 
 Creating Issue Return 
 Issue 
 Return 
 In

 Transfer 
 Transfer refers

 efficient logistics. 
 Why is Transfer Important? 
 The

 or locations. It ensures that stock levels are managed accurately, reduces 
 the risk of shortages, and optimises the use of available inventory across 
 the entire organisation. 
 When is Transfer Used? 
 The Transfer

 to another within the same business unit. This could happen for several

title: Bill Inward
text:
Bill Inward 
 Help > Accounts Payable" />
 Bill Inward 
 Bill Inward refers 
 to the process of acknowledging and recording a bill received from a vendor 
 within the system to ensure that it is accounted for and not misplaced. 
 It involves verifying the details of the bill, confirming its receipt, 
 and processing it for further action, such as payment or approval. 
 Benefits of Creating a Bill Inward 
 Efficiency: The 
 process streamlines the bill processing for workflow, reducing manual 
 errors and saving time in handling bills. 
 Transparency: It 
 provides visibility into the status of bills, ensuring that they are acknowledged 
 and accounted for promptly. 
 Compliance: It 
 helps to maintain accurate financial records and ensure that they are 
 acknowledged and accounted for promptly. 
 Supplier Relationships: It 
 can improve relationships with suppliers by ensuring timely acknowledgement 
 and processing of bills, leading to smoother transactions. 
 Use Case 
 In 
 a construction company, the accounts department receives invoices from 
 various suppliers for materials delivered to the construction site. Without 
 a proper bill inward process, there is a risk of invoices being misplaced 
 or not reaching the accounts department for processing. This could lead 
 to delays in payment to suppliers and, in turn, cause disruptions in the 
 supply chain. 
 By 
 implementing a bill inward system, as soon as a bill is received from 
 a supplier, it is acknowledged in the system, verified for accuracy, and 
 processed for payment or approval. This ensures that all bills are accounted 
 for, payments are made on time, and supplier relationships are maintained. 
 Thus, there is a chance of avoiding potential delays in the material supply 
 due to unresolved billing issues. 
 Steps to Perform Bill Inward for Brokerage

 Navigate

 Vendor Bank 
 Update 
 This feature allows suppliers or vendors 
 to update their bank details using a designated menu. This functionality

 accurately and efficiently. 
 When is this important? 
 Vendors should 
 update their bank details in several situations. 
 Firstly, when 
 they switch to a new bank or open a new account, it is essential to update 
 the information to avoid any payment disruptions. 
 Secondly, if 
 there are changes to the existing bank account details, such as a new 
 account number or branch, these updates should be made promptly. 
 Lastly, vendors 
 may need to update their bank details upon request or as part of a scheduled 
 update process to maintain accurate records.

title: Payment Requisition
text:
Payment Requisition 
 Help > Accounts Payable" />
 Payment 
 Requisition 
 A Payment Requisition is a formal request 
 made by the purchase team to the accounts team, asking for payment to 
 be made for the purchase of materials. 
 Why is Payment Requisition Important? 
 The Payment Requisition is important 
 because it ensures that the accounts team is aware of the payment needs 
 and can process the payment in a timely manner. This helps maintain good 
 relationships with suppliers and ensures the smooth operation of the purchasing 
 process. 
 When is Payment Requisition Applicable? 
 The Payment Requisition should be submitted 
 as soon as the purchase team needs to make a payment for materials. This 
 typically happens after the materials have been received and the invoice/work 
 order has been verified. 
 Steps to Create a Payment Requsition 
 Choose the preferred Business Unit, 
 Document Type, Financial Year, Account Head, and Order No. These fields 
 are mandatory to fill. 
 Under Document type there are 
 multiple options available. However, the user needs to select only one 
 option: 
 · Payment Requisition (PREQ): 
 A formal request for payment to be 
 made for a purchase or service.

 after saving the entry

 are 4 options available:

 Payment made in advance before the receipt of goods or services.

 Ledger / Sub Ledger (Normal): Standard 
 adjustments recorded in the general or sub-ledger accounts.

 head

 parent account head gets displayed

 entered 
 However, we will only select the ‘On 
 A/c’ or ‘Bill’ option, as applicable in this context. 
 Under Entry Type , there are 4 
 options available. However, we are only going to choose the following 
 option in this context: 
 · Purchase Order: Entry related to an order placed for purchasing goods 
 or services. 
 The Parent 
 Account Head field will be auto populated. 
 Once the above data 
 is filled, click on Add New Row . The following screen will be visible. 
 In this screen, the Parent Account

 Enter the Amount for which the

 Once done, click on Next .

 Once done click on Next .

 Quotation 
 When a user creates any enquiry or Request 
 for Quotation (RFQ), a quotation is automatically generated. This quotation 
 is then visible to the supplier in their portal. 
 When is this important? 
 · Upon Enquiry or RFQ Creation: 
 A quotation is automatically generated 
 whenever a user creates an enquiry or RFQ, ensuring immediate availability 
 for the supplier. 
 · Supplier Review: Suppliers should review the quotations in their portal 
 regularly to stay updated on new enquiries and RFQs. 
 · Before Sending Proposals: 
 Suppliers can use the information 
 in the quotations to prepare and send accurate proposals or responses. 
 · Regular Monitoring: Regularly monitor the portal for new 
 quotations to ensure timely responses and maintain good business relationships. 
 Navigation Path 
 Supplier Portal> Tendering> Quotation 
 Steps to update Quotation 
 1. Choose the preferred entry from the 
 grid. 
 2. Click on Edit. 
 3. Move to the Item info tab and update

 4. Keep clicking Next until you reach Finish 
 and finally Submit. 
 Once the quotation is updated, the details

 Now, the Farvision user can do the price 
 comparison based on the updated quotation sent by the supplier.

title: ASN
text:
ASN 
 Help > Supplier Portal > Shipment" />
 ASN 
 An ASN (Advance Shipment Note) refers 
 to a Goods Receipt Note (GRN) entry. It allows suppliers to view pending 
 Purchase Orders (POs) project-wise and select the relevant items when 
 sending materials to the company. Based on this entry, a GRN is automatically 
 created. 
 When is this important? 
 · Before Shipment : Suppliers should 
 create an ASN before shipping materials to the company to ensure all relevant 
 items are documented. 
 · Upon Receiving POs : When suppliers 
 receive new POs, they should review and select the items to be shipped, 
 creating an ASN for those items. 
 · Project-Specific Shipments: 
 For project-specific shipments, suppliers 
 should use the ASN to ensure that the correct materials are sent for each 
 project. 
 · Regular Updates : Regularly update 
 ASNs to reflect any changes in the shipment or PO status, maintaining 
 accurate records.

title: Material Classification and Coding System
text:
Material Classification and Coding System 
 Tutorial" />
 Material 
 Classification and Coding System 
 Codification of 
 materials can also be termed as the identification of materials. This 
 deals with uniquely identifying each item in the inventory. Unique identification 
 of the materials (whether they are raw materials, work-in-process or finished 
 goods) is the first step towards a good materials management system. 
 In 
 Farvision Material modules, material master data refers to all the material 
 master records, which are stored in the Farvision system. The material 
 master is the central source of information for a material related to 
 several application areas (Purchasing, storage, accounting, sales, etc.) 
 based on material type. 
 Material 
 Master Data 
 The key points 
 to note about material master data are as follows: 
 This is the enterprise 
 main source of material-specific data. This data will include information 
 on the materials that a company can procure, produce, store, or sell. 
 Since there are different departments in an enterprise and each department 
 works on some specific material, they will enter different information 
 regarding their material. So, each user department has its own view of 
 the material master record. The data screens that are used to create material 
 master can be divided into two categories − 
 Main 
 Data − this will include basic data (base unit of measure, weight), 
 purchasing data (over tolerance and under tolerance), accounting data 
 (standard price, moving price). 
 Additional 
 Data − this will include additional information like long description, 
 specification, brand about material etc. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Supply Chain Management
text:
Supply Chain Management 
 Tutorial" />
 Supply Chain Management 
 Supply Chain Management 
 is for co-ordination of people, properties, processes, vendors, information 
 and resources to services to the end customer. 
 Supply Chain Management 
 can be done effectively with technology. The ERP software solutions are 
 well equipped with advanced analytics tools that analyze data from all 
 departments of business. ERP can be used to create a more agile enterprise 
 that can take decisions proactively to maximize business results. 
 Procurement & Planning : 
 The Real estate companies can use the software to manage the various property 
 listings for rentals & sales etc. The software can be used to analyze 
 the demand for properties in various locations, their pricing, investment 
 information etc. 
 The ERP Software 
 minimizes the gap between demand and supply for items. The optimized procurement 
 is in line with the planned goals and milestones. The ERP system helps 
 companies to operate with optimal inventory to reduce capital expenditure. 
 At the same time, it ensures that all ongoing projects smooth effectively. 
 Documentation & File 
 Management : The documents associated with 
 the properties can be managed using the ERP System. Real estate companies 
 and organizations use document 
 management and digitization for meeting compliance needs without 
 hassles. 
 Purchase Orders & 
 Vendor management : 
 Can automate purchase order creation, approvals, payments, performance 
 management for vendors. Once the purchase orders are created, the payments 
 for vendors can be done against milestones. Companies are in a better 
 position to negotiation with vendors; leverage bulk discounts and also 
 manage vendor payments transparently . 
 Projects Development : Real 
 estate companies typically manage multiple properties and sites. Many 
 a times, they also have to look at ongoing property developments and construction. 
 Even when these projects are outsourced to other developers, the execution 
 can be tracked. 
 Managing Warehouse : Companies 
 need a state of the art solution for managing their warehousing (The space 
 utilization, consumption trends and availability of raw material for ongoing 
 projects etc.). An ERP system can track multiple warehouse locations, 
 transportation channels and streamline logistics for companies . 
 Managing Compliance : System 
 provides an effective workflow system for getting these approvals in order. 
 When projects are planned, the tax implications on sourcing, developments 
 and services need to be analyzed carefully. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: Inventory Valuation
text:
Inventory Valuation 
 Tutorial" />
 Inventory Valuation 
 An inventory valuation allows 
 a company to provide a monetary 
 value for items that make up their inventory . 
 Inventories are usually the largest current asset of 
 a business, and proper measurement of them is necessary to assure accurate financial 
 statements . If inventory is not properly measured, expenses and revenues cannot 
 be properly matched with financial books. 
 Inventory 
 Accounting System 
 Perpetual Inventory : 
 The perpetual 
 inventory system requires accounting records to show the 
 amount of inventory on hand at all times. It maintains a separate 
 account in the subsidiary ledger for 
 each good in stock, and the account is updated each time a quantity 
 is added or taken out. 
 Periodic 
 Inventory : 
 In the periodic inventory system, 
 sales are recorded as they occur but the inventory is not updated. 
 A physical inventory must be 
 taken at the end of the year to determine the cost of goods. 
 Methods 
 of Valuation – 
 There are three types of inventory valuation methods, but mostly two methods 
 are used for Real Estate Industries as described below. 
 First-in-first-out 
 (FIFO) inventory valuation 
 Average 
 cost (AC) inventory valuation 
 Types 
 of Valuation explained : 
 First-in-first-out (FIFO) 
 inventory valuation : 
 Under this method, materials which are received first are also to 
 be issued first. In other words, the pricing of the issue of the first 
 lot is done at the cost at which that lot was acquired. As such, the 
 closing inventories are valued at latest purchase price and, thus, 
 it will represent current condition as far as possible. 
 Average cost (AC) inventory 
 valuation: Under this Method, cost is calculated by adding 
 different prices and, thereafter, divided by the total number of purchases. 
 It is assumed that the cost of inventory is based on the average cost 
 of the goods available during the period. 
 Warehouse wise 
 Valuation explained: 
 1. 
 First-in-first-out (FIFO) inventory valuation : If material 
 issued through warehouse to project and if valuation method is FIFO, then 
 amount will be calculated on the basis of the example explained below. 
 Example: If 10 quantity of item purchased 
 in April @ Rs.100, 20 quantity of item purchased in July @ Rs.105 and 
 30 quantity of item purchased in Dec @ Rs.110, then total 60 quantity 
 (10+20+30) of item purchased during the year, then value of goods would 
 be showing in inventory as per FIFO based is Rs.6400 based on the following 
 formula: 
 Formula is {(10*100) 
 + (20*105) + (30*110)}. 
 2. Average cost (AC) inventory 
 valuation: If 
 material issued through warehouse to project and if valuation method is 
 Average cost basis, then amount will be calculated on the basis of the 
 example explained below. 
 Example: If 
 10 quantity of item purchased in April @ Rs.100, 20 quantity of item purchased 
 in July @ Rs.105 and 30 quantity of item purchased in Dec @ Rs.110, then 
 total 60 quantity (10+20+30) of item purchased during the year, then value 
 of goods would be showing in inventory as per Average cost based is Rs.6300 
 based on the following formula: 
 Formula is ( 100+105+110 ) so average 
 cost is Rs 105. 
 3

 users need to create separate Extra Charges type of Documents from the 
 Administration Module. 
 3. 
 Creation of Goods Receipt Note against Purchase Order 
 Menu Path: 
 Material -> Receiving -> Goods 
 Receipt Note 
 Creation 
 of Partial Goods Receipt Note against the Purchase Order 
 As 
 the Extra Charges details already defined in the Purchase Order where 
 calculation basis was mentioned as Quantity based, hence during creation 
 of Goods Receipt Note against those extra charges amount also auto calculated 
 based on the GRN quantity. 
 4. Creation of Purchase Bill against Goods Receipt 
 Note 
 Menu 
 Path: Material -> Accounts Payable -> Purchase 
 Bill 
 5. Generation of Extra Charges Bill from the Non 
 Stores Purchase 
 Menu 
 Path: Material -> Accounts Payable -> Non 
 Stores Purchase 
 For 
 Booking of Extra Charges Bill users need to select the Extra Charges GRN 
 type from the Link With 
 option. 
 To 
 tag the Pending Extra Charges details against the same Vendor users need 
 to click on Extra Charges 
 – From GRN option. 
 After 
 tagging of Extra Charges document number under Posting 
 Info tab required Ledger and Amount details will auto appear and 
 there is no manual intervention required. 
 Required 
 Statutory details need to be mentioned in the Billing 
 Term Info Tab for generating the Extra Charges Bill.

title: Configuration
text:
Configuration 
 Mobile App > FV Approval" />
 Configuration Process 
 Mobile Configuration 
 Mobile configuration is required for each mobile app (both IOS and android) to enable push notifications. For details about Enterprise Name, server public IP and app credentials, please refer to the detailed help on Mobile Configuration . 
 Download Farvision Approval App from 
 1. Apple Apps Store (For IOS) 
 2. Android Store (For Android) 
 Please type FV Approval on Google Play Store/Apple Apps Store to find and download the mobile application or download from the following URLs 
 Download Links 
 For IOS 
 https://apps.apple.com/in/app/farvisionapprovalr2/id1435066074 
 For Android 
 https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gamut.farvisionapprovalr2&hl=en_IN&gl=US 
 Cloud SetUp 
 Step1: Install and open FV Approval App. Press 'Configure Your App' to setup your account. 
 Step2: Press ‘Cloud SetUp’ if your Farvision application runs on Farvision Cloud server. Please contact your administrator to know your cloud server name. Choose your cloud server from “Cloud SetUp” option. 
 Step3: After account configuration, enter ‘User Name’ and ‘Password’ and press ‘Login’. 
 OR 
 Set Up 
 Step1: Install and open FV Approval App. Press 'Configure Your App' to setup your account. Press ‘Set Up’. 
 Step2 : Enter your Enterprise name and on premises server URL/IP. HTTPS is required to be checked if your server is SSL certified and you have entered domain name. If you have entered IP Address as server url then SSL is not required hence left this unchecked. 
 Step3: After account configuration, enter ‘User Name’ and ‘Password’ and press ‘Login’. 
 © 
 Gamut Infosystems Limited

title: FAQ
text:
Frequently Asked Questions 
 Frequently 
 Asked Questions 
 1. How to do the 
 Setup of Supplier related to Import Purchase? 
 Answer: Change the GST 
 state as Export, Open Financial > Setup > Account head, now 
 search the specific account head & click on GSTIN Info. 
 2. What could 
 be the cause of encountering an error ‘NSP Error_BUDGET NOT found ‘ , and how can this issue be resolved? 
 Answer: This issue is 
 because the Sub Project and Budget has been set as mandatory in Metadata, 
 but the same haven't been entered in the 'Posting Info’ during the 
 NSP (Non Store Purchase) entry. 
 Note, that if you want to remove the mandatory option it should be 
 adjusted from Administration > Database > Metadata. 
 3. What might 
 be the reason for encountering a warning message while creating a code 
 under Vendor Onboarding system, and how can it be addressed? 
 Answer: 
 This warning message is because 
 the email entered in the 'Contact Person Info' tab is already given 
 in another Account Head. Rectify the same and then proceed. 
 4. How can the 
 error "Valuation will be mismatch due to back date entry" be 
 resolved when attempting to delete a Goods Receipt Note (GRN) entry? 
 Answer: When attempting 
 to delete a GRN (Goods Receipt Note) entry, an error may occur stating 
 "Valuation will be mismatch due to back date entry." To 
 address this issue, it is recommended to check the stock summary for 
 the same Business Unit (BU), warehouse, and item. Try deleting the 
 entries starting from the last one in the sequence, including GRN, 
 Issue, ILTO, Transfer, Sales bill, and Stock Adjustment, to ensure 
 consistency in valuation. 
 5. What could be the reasons behind a blank 
 Purchase Order (PO) number and the display of the date as 1980 in the 
 Indent TO BILL Report? 
 Answer: If the PO is 
 not created against the Indent in that case during the generation 
 of the Indent To Bill report; PO Column will be blank and PO Date 
 will be 1980. 
 6. What steps should be taken to address 
 the inability to edit specific items in the Item Master? 
 Answer: It is recommended to check 
 whether a Business Rule is active for the Item Master in the Administration 
 module. If a Business Rule is active, ensure that Post Approval rights 
 are granted to resolve the issue. 
 7. How can you resolve the issue of missing 
 item master details description in a PO entry? 
 Answer: If the detailed description 
 of an item is not populating during PO entry, ensure that you click 
 the 'Green box' located at the right side of the 'Detail Description' 
 field in the Item Info tab in PO entry. 
 8. How to resolve a situation where the users 
 are unable to edit Non Store Purchase? 
 Answer: The inability 
 to edit the Non Store Purchase (NSP) entry is due to an existing Receipt/Payment 
 entry already being tagged with the specified NSP entry. Once a receipt 
 or payment entry is made against an NSP entry, editing the NSP entry 
 becomes restricted. Users are advised to verify the related transactions 
 and make adjustments accordingly. 
 9. How to address 
 the mismatch between Indent Stock at the time of print and Stock Summary 
 Report? 
 Answer: 
 To address the mismatch between Indent Stock (at the time of print) 
 and the Stock Summary Report, it is important to verify the accuracy 
 of the current stock during the Indent entry. Stock showing at the 
 time of printing in Indent is saved at the time of entry. So the current 
 stock may differ from the one shown in Indent Stock (at the time of 
 print). 
 10. How to resolve the Stock mismatch in 
 Warehouse Reports (Stock summary and Stock summary with warehouse)? 
 Answer: 
 This mismatch arises because warehouse-wise valuation is not specified; 
 only the today's rate is displayed in the warehouse-wise context. 
 The absence of today's rate for an item can result from the lack of 
 closing value for that item on the current date. In that case stock 
 summary value will be a real value and stock summary with warehouse 
 value will show an Approx value. 
 11. Is it possible to create a duplicate Indent / PO? 
 Answer: Yes, there is an option to Copy Template 
 from where you can copy the respective Indent / PO. 
 12. What are the 
 criteria that can cause a work order to be created but not displayed in 
 non-store purchase? 
 Answer: These 
 criteria include: 
 1. Work 
 order document date must be equal or less than the current date. 
 2. 
 2.The completion date for the work order must be equal to or 
 less than the current date. 
 3. 3.Work 
 order being provisional (unapproved). 
 4. Any work order 
 type other than Service Work Order will not be shown. 
 13. 
 How 
 can mandatory file attachments be implemented in PO? 
 Answer : To do this, you can access the DMS 
 – Attachment Setup from the Administration module. 
 14. 
 Can a PO 
 of 100 be closed with the bill of 30, even though the GRN indicates receiving 
 40? 
 Answer: 
 No, it is not possible to short 
 close the PO with the bill of 30 because the GRN is already tagged 
 with 40.
